name: Havasupai Falls
unique: Turquoise waterfalls in a side canyon of the Grand Canyon, reachable only by a ten mile hike or a helicopter, on tribal land with a village of 200 people.
buzz: Permits are a lottery and people plan a year out; the hike out in heat is the hard part. Pack light and pay for the mule.

name: Grand Canyon Mule Ride
unique: Descend the Bright Angel Trail on a mule to Phantom Ranch at the bottom of the canyon, sleep in a cabin and ride out the next day.
buzz: The mules know the trail better than you; reviews warn about saddle soreness and the weight limit is enforced. Book a year ahead.

name: Antelope Canyon
unique: A slot canyon carved into swirling sandstone, where a shaft of light hits the floor at midday and the walls glow orange, pink and purple.
buzz: The photography tour is worth the extra; the standard tour is rushed. Book months ahead and respect Navajo rules.

name: Monument Valley
unique: The red sandstone buttes and mesas that defined the Western film, on Navajo land, with a 17-mile dirt loop and guided tours to areas you cannot drive.
buzz: The loop drive is spectacular and the guided tour goes deeper; the light at dawn and dusk is the reason photographers come.

name: Canyon de Chelly
unique: A red sandstone canyon still farmed and lived in by Navajo families, with 1,000-year old cliff dwellings and a white house ruin you can hike to without a guide.
buzz: The rim drives are free and stunning; the canyon floor requires a Navajo guide and is worth it. Fewer crowds than the Grand Canyon.

name: Arizona Sonora Desert Museum
unique: Part zoo, part botanical garden, part natural history museum, with hummingbirds landing on your hand and a cave you walk through in the dark.
buzz: People call it the best desert museum in the world; go at opening in summer and take the hummingbird aviary.

name: Sedona Vortex Hike
unique: Red sandstone spires and juniper forests at sites believed to concentrate energy, with hikes to Cathedral Rock and Airport Mesa that are gorgeous regardless of your metaphysics.
buzz: Believers and skeptics both love the landscape; sunrise at Cathedral Rock is crowded. Parking passes are required.

name: Kartchner Caverns
unique: A living cave discovered in 1974 and developed with airlocks and misters to protect it, with a 58-foot column and straws that are still growing.
buzz: The conservation story is as good as the formations; tours are timed and photography is limited. Book ahead.

name: Biosphere 2
unique: A 3.1-acre sealed glass ecosystem where eight people lived for two years, now a research facility with an ocean, a rainforest and a savanna under glass.
buzz: The human experiment story is fascinating and the building is a monument to 1990s hubris; tours are well led.

name: Bearizona
unique: A drive through wildlife park with black bears, wolves and bison roaming large forest enclosures, plus a walk through section with otters and jaguars.
buzz: The drive through is the draw and the bears come close to the car; the walk through is smaller. A good stop on the way to the Grand Canyon.

name: Meteor Crater
unique: A one mile-wide impact crater left by a 150-foot asteroid 50,000 years ago, with an Apollo training site and a guided rim tour.
buzz: It is more impressive than photos suggest; the museum is good and the wind is constant. A classic Route 66 stop.

name: Mystery Castle
unique: An 18 room castle built from stone, adobe and salvage by a father for his daughter, with a chapel, a dungeon and furniture made from railroad parts.
buzz: The story is better than the building and the guides tell it well; it is hidden at the base of South Mountain.

name: Rooster Cogburn Ostrich Ranch
unique: An ostrich ranch beside the interstate where you hand feed ostriches, donkeys and parakeets from a cup, with a monster truck tour and a petting area.
buzz: It is silly and cheap and kids talk about it for years; the birds are aggressive in a funny way. A good break on the drive to Tucson.

name: Tombstone Gunfight
unique: The actual O.K. Corral site, with daily reenactments of the 30-second gunfight that killed three men, plus the Bird Cage Theatre and Boot Hill.
buzz: The reenactment is corny and fun; the historians are better than the show. The town is unapologetically a tourist trap and owns it.
